one_liner: Archived pure-Rust Opus CELT-only codec (48 kHz); encodes 1-2% faster than trunk libopus at 5 ms, 192-320 kb/s.
what_it_does: A safe-Rust reimplementation of the CELT half of Opus: an Encoder and Decoder for 48 kHz mono or stereo CELT-only fullband packets (2.5/5/10/20 ms frames, CBR, constrained VBR or an exact byte budget), plus packet parsing, repacketizing and soft-clip helpers. The API is its own Rust interface (Encoder::new, set_bitrate, set_vbr, encode_i16/i24/f32 and their _into variants that reuse packet storage, Decoder::decode_*_into), with no C API. Packets carry a standard Opus TOC byte and interoperate with libopus, but the encoder output is not byte-identical to libopus. SILK, hybrid, Ogg Opus, PLC/FEC and sample rates other than 48 kHz are not implemented.
how_it_is_fast: It is a close port of libopus's CELT pipeline (MDCT, PVQ/CWRS band quantization, energy coding, pitch prefilter and the tonality analysis) in safe Rust using the `wide` SIMD crate. Profiler-chosen unsafe kernels sit behind checked wrappers in an in-tree crate: an AVX2/FMA pitch correlation with a static tail mask, unchecked-index MDCT rotations, a pulse-cache lookup, a stereo 24-bit deemphasis kernel and an AArch64 NEON radix-5 FFT. Allocation-free scratch buffers do the rest. Each of these changes was accepted by an alternating A/B and was worth about 0.1-0.7%. Part of the margin is less work or different builds, not better code. The Rust analysis port leaves out libopus's MLP/GRU speech/music classifier (compute_dense/compute_gru in analysis.c). The i16 decode path hard-clamps instead of soft-clipping. Rust was built with -C target-cpu=native, ThinLTO and one codegen unit, while the libopus.a build flags were not recorded.
when_to_use: Pure-Rust builds that cannot link C and need 48 kHz stereo music encoding at 192-320 kb/s with 5 ms frames (low-latency streaming), with measured quality parity to trunk libopus: ViSQOL MOS-LQO 4.5731 vs 4.5724 on 240 round trips.
Signed 24-bit pipelines: encode_i24/decode_i24 take sign-extended i32 samples directly, so audio never passes through 16-bit PCM.
Projects that require #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in the codec crate itself; all unsafe code sits in a separate audited kernel crate with documented invariants (SAFETY.md).
As reference code for the successor wavey-ai/soundkit (soundkit-opus 0.13.0 on crates.io), which carries the same codec, newer fixes and the corrected decoder measurement.
when_not_to_use: Speech or low-bitrate VoIP (SILK/hybrid), sample rates other than 48 kHz, Ogg Opus files, packet-loss concealment, FEC, multistream or multi-frame packets: the decoder returns Error::Unimplemented for anything but single-frame fullband CELT-only packets.

If you want faster decoding: the author's 2026-08-25 correction (soundkit-opus report) found the 1.50-4.64% decode lead came from timing each decoder on its own encoder's packets. On identical packets (i24, 192 kb/s constrained VBR) Rust was +0.51% slower on C packets, -0.30% on Rust packets and +0.10% combined, which is parity.

Other frame sizes or bitrates: no current numbers exist outside the 5 ms, 192-320 kb/s cells. The README's older full-matrix snapshot on a synthetic fixture had Rust slower in nearly every cell (often 10-65% on encode and 50-160% on decode). In the browser WASM comparison, Rust encoding was slower than libopusjs (81-82x vs 110.9x realtime at 128 kb/s).
Production deployments: the repo is archived, both crates.io releases are yanked, and the README calls the encoder experimental and 'not production replacements for libopus'.
Non-x86 hosts: the native result covers one Xeon Platinum 8581C only; the report says AArch64 and WASM parity are not established.

integration.form: crate (rlib/cdylib; optional wasm feature via wasm-bindgen; an npm/WASM build exists)
integration.dependencies: wide 0.7; in-tree path crate libopus-rs-kernels (publish = false); optional wasm-bindgen 0.2
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2021; no MSRV declared; the benchmark used Rust 1.97.1
integration.platforms: any Rust target with scalar fallbacks; x86-64 AVX2+FMA pitch kernel (runtime-checked), AArch64 NEON FFT kernel, wasm32 simd128 build; measured only on x86-64
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Encoder and Decoder are owned values used through &mut self, and the CELT mode tables are shared immutable statics

gotchas: Both crates.io releases (0.0.1 and 0.0.2) are yanked, and 0.0.2 (2026-06-30) predates the kernel crate and the August optimizations. Building from git needs the in-tree crates/libopus-rs-kernels path crate; for new work, use soundkit-opus.

decode_i16 converts with a hard clamp (float_to_i16), while libopus's opus_decode in float builds soft-clips (OPTIONAL_CLIP=1; opus_decode24 does not). Output differs on hot masters, and the extra C pass is consistent with the 16-bit decode lead (3.55-4.64%) being about twice the 24-bit one (1.50-1.97%).

The 'packet identity gate' is weak. packet_checksum hashes only each packet's length and first and last bytes, and the decode checksum sums 3 samples per frame. Mid-payload changes from a speed patch would go undetected, and the report uses this gate to carry the earlier full-length quality pass forward to the final binaries.

The only encoder controls are bitrate, VBR and an experimental direct-cubic mode. There is no complexity, bandwidth, signal or DTX setter, and the encoder always runs the maximum-complexity path. Direct-cubic packets are not decodable by standard Opus decoders.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over opus-pure, ruopus, opus-rs or ropus only for 48 kHz stereo music at 192-320 kb/s with 5 ms frames, 24-bit I/O and published perceptual-parity data against trunk libopus. Even then, prefer its successor soundkit-opus. Those siblings implement SILK/hybrid and claim larger margins against libopus 1.6.1 or 1.5.2, and opuspp is the C++ choice for decode speed.
verified_claims_summary: Encode: on four 10 s excerpts from a private music corpus (48 kHz stereo CELT, 5 ms frames, complexity 10, 16- and 24-bit, CBR and constrained VBR at 192/256/320 kb/s), Rust used 1.19-2.36% less time than trunk libopus 03647f5. The C side was a static libopus.a with an unrecorded configure, driven through opus_encode with OPUS_APPLICATION_AUDIO. The run used one GCP c4-highcpu-4 Xeon Platinum 8581C pinned to CPU 2, with three alternating rounds of seven repeats. Decode results moved between checkpoints with no decoder change, which the report calls normal variance: about 0.5 points weighted and about 1 point at the ends of the per-cell range, the same order as the encode margin. The catalogued 1.50-4.64% decode lead is superseded by the author's same-packet re-test, which shows parity (+0.10%).
status_note: Archived on 2026-08-25 with 0 stars, both crates.io versions yanked and no issues filed. The BSD-3-Clause code can be vendored from git, but development and the corrected results moved to wavey-ai/soundkit (soundkit-opus 0.13.0, MIT AND BSD-3-Clause).
